newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended lower at 8.2948 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Wednesday on a technical correction after hitting a 10-week high of 8.2938 on Tuesday, traders said.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2949.
Dealers said the yuan's rise on Tuesday was partly due to speculative buying in late trading and that a correction on Wednesday was expected.
The yuan opened down at 8.2943 and moved steadily in a range of 8.2940 and 8.2948 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2950 and a high of 8.2899.
Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2946, traders said.

One dealer said both buyers and sellers were reluctant to trade heavily before a three-day break ahead of the Labour Day holiday and the weekend. The market will be closed from Thursday to Saturday with trading resuming on Sunday.
"The holiday made trading dull and the yuan was stuck in a narrow range," he added.
A second dealer said that despite the day's fall, pro-yuan sentiment was strong, which kept the yuan above the key 8.2950 level for the whole session.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move up slightly on Sunday.
The yuan closed up at 6.5290 from 6.5360 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0713 from 1.0698 against the Hong Kong dollar.
